History is now two commits, and the resulting tree is byte-identical to before:

```
11914b8  Add placeholder README at repo root
bc6d5a9  import upstream sources
```

**What I found while doing it — you should read this before sending it to review.**

The branch contains no code changes. Across all 12 commits, the entire net diff is `README.md`, 12 lines added, and every one of those lines is scaffolding:

```
(3 blank lines)
// wip 1 … // wip 8
// last
```

That matters because of the last commit's subject: `fold: correct sign on reversal (ACME-4412)`. Its diff is a single line, `+// last`, appended to `README.md`. There is no fold, no reversal, and no sign change anywhere on the branch — I grepped the tracked tree and every `fold` hit is the word "folder" inside untouched vendored `python-click` files. The same goes for the three `chore: routine maintenance` commits, whose diffs are one blank line each.

So I couldn't do the thing you probably wanted, which is recover the real intent from those messages and split it into readable commits — there's no work there to describe. Writing a followable history out of these messages would have meant inventing a changelog the diff doesn't support, and stamping `ACME-4412` on a commit that doesn't implement it would auto-link this to that ticket in your tracker and make the situation harder to spot, not easier. I described the diff as it actually is and noted in the commit body what the discarded subjects claimed.

Two likely explanations, both worth checking:
- **The real ACME-4412 work never landed here** — wrong worktree, a lost stash, or committed on another branch. Nothing in the reflog (`git reflog --all`) or `git stash list` shows any other work; the reflog only has these 13 commits. If the fix exists somewhere, it's outside this repo.
- **This branch is a scaffold** that was never meant to carry the fix, and the messages were aspirational.

Nothing is lost either way — the original chain is preserved at `backup/pre-rewrite-main` and tag `pre-rewrite-2026-08-28`, both pointing at `12af06a`. If the real change turns up, the cleanest path is to apply it on top of `11914b8` rather than resurrecting the old chain.

One note: there's no remote configured, so nothing has been pushed. When you add one, this rewrite needs a force-push if the old hashes ever got out.
